Abstract
                Background
                Implementing the health information system (HIS) is more complex and costly than implementing other information systems. The present study was conducted to design and evaluate technical requirements for the HIS.
              
                Methods
                The present study was conducted in 2016 by determining technical requirements for the HIS using the Delphi technique and then evaluating this system using a checklist based on the approved requirements.
              
                Results
                The first part of the study designed a 73-item final list of technical requirements for the HIS in four domains, i.e. communication service, system architecture, security service and system response time. The evaluation results obtained in the second part showed that communication service was met in 63.8% of the HIS programs, system architecture in 65.5%, security service in 72.4% and system response time in 76.3%.
              
                Conclusions
                A technical evaluation tool was designed and used to select and evaluate the HIS. The evaluation results suggested the study HIS was poorer in terms of communication service and system architecture than in the other two dimensions.

result.paraphrase:
Abstract

Background
Compared with other information systems, implementing a health information system (HIS) is more complex and expensive. This study was carried out to develop and assess the HIS’s technical requirements.

Methods
In 2016, technical requirements for the HIS were identified using the Delphi method, and the system was then assessed with a checklist derived from the approved requirements.

Results
The first stage produced a final 73-item set of HIS technical requirements across four areas: communication service, system architecture, security service, and system response time. In the second stage, evaluation showed that communication service was satisfied in 63.8% of HIS programs, system architecture in 65.5%, security service in 72.4%, and system response time in 76.3%.

Conclusions
A technical evaluation instrument was created and applied to select and assess the HIS. The results indicated that the study HIS performed worse in communication service and system architecture than in the other two dimensions.
